claim: History, not a forecast. Nursing care facility prices (producer price index, Dec 1994 to Mar 2026) rose 3.52% a year over the whole period; over the 136 overlapping 20-year stretches they rose between 2.78% and 3.61% a year (median 3.1%). A daily benefit that started out covering the full daily price would, 20 years later, cover a median 54.3% with no inflation option, 98.1% with 3% compound (range 88.9% to 104.4%; full coverage in 44.1% of stretches) and 144.1% with 5% compound (never below 130.6%). In this price record the 3% option came close to keeping pace and the 5% option ran well ahead of prices in every stretch.

numbers.definition: Number of 20-year windows. 20-year window = start month s (1994-12-01 .. 2006-03-01) and end month e = s + 240 months; price ratio P = PPI(e)/PPI(s). Coverage for a benefit growing at compound rate r = 100 x (1+r)^20 / P (a benefit that paid 100% of the daily price at s). PPI = PCU623110623110, Producer Price Index by Industry: Nursing Care Facilities, index Dec 1994=100, not seasonally adjusted, monthly, pinned FRED CSV with coed=2026-03-01 (observations 1994-12-01 .. 2026-03-01).

assumptions: The policy's daily benefit starts equal to the daily price of care at the start of the window and grows by r compounded annually (r = 0, 3% or 5%) for 20 years.

Nursing care prices are measured by the national producer price index for nursing care facilities (what facilities receive per unit of service, all payers), which is a stand-in for the private-pay daily rate a policyholder faces.
Overlapping monthly start dates; the index begins in Dec 1994, so only starts from Dec 1994 to Mar 2006 have a full 20 years.
Data pinned at Mar 2026 because the most recent PPI months are preliminary and revised for four months.
Premium differences between the options and premium increases on in-force policies are not modeled.
